content.text: Single continuous cinematic camera move, no cuts. Stylised high-end 3D illustration, cinematic but deliberately not photorealistic. Deep violet and midnight-blue base, structures and light in royal and electric violet. Warm orange sunset light used only as backlight, rim light and highlights, never dominant. Soft bloom, volumetric haze, shallow depth of field, subtle film grain, calm slightly surreal atmosphere. Organic surfaces meet digital light structures. No comic look, no neon cyberpunk city, no text, no letters, no logos, no signage. The mossy violet branch fills the frame, its fine lattice dim and dormant. The camera pushes in slowly along the branch toward the hollow at the centre of its curve. A dragonfly glides in from the upper right: a precision-engineered machine with a dark chrome and anodised violet segmented body, fine articulated legs, large faceted eyes, and two pairs of long transparent wings whose veining is a lattice of glowing violet nodes and lines, edges catching warm orange rim light - elegant, calm, constructed, never cute and never cartoonish. It draws a fine luminous violet trail behind it as it flies. It hovers briefly and settles into the hollow. The instant its legs touch, a violet impulse ignites beneath it and the dormant lattice on the branch wakes up: bright nodes and light lines race outward along the bark in both directions, run up the flower stalks, and motes of light lift off the surface. Nothing is added to the branch - the structure that was already there begins to glow. As the light spreads, the camera drifts around the dragonfly in a slow half-orbit, passing her side and briefly seeing her from the front against the sunset, then swinging back in behind her. Then the dragonfly lifts off and flies forward over the darkening landscape. The camera falls in behind her and follows. The camera never pulls back and never loses the dragonfly. The shot ends with the dragonfly clearly in frame ahead of the camera, seen from behind, both settling into a slow steady forward drift, the silhouette of a modern building far ahead on the horizon.
